question_en: What is the specific name of the instrument in the figure?
gold_trajectory:
# Detailed Simulated Retrieval Trajectory · 2-2-D01

## Step 01 · Understand the complete manual apparatus by mentally reassociating the perforated plates with it

**Action:** Observe the connection relationship between the main body and accessories in the current input, then attempt search combinations such as `grain seed cutter perforated plates hand lever`, `farinotome plaques`, or `Kornschneider Vergleichsplatten`.

**Evidence Observation:** The main body features scissor-style long handles, a hinge joint, a flip-up cover plate, and a rectangular perforated working area, with three separate dark perforated plates placed beside it. The detachable plates and the metal clamping/cutting mechanism should be interpreted together; one should not directly identify it as a microtiter plate simply because of the dense hole array, nor is it necessary to count holes one by one from a perspective view first. The complete structure is more suitable for searching within clamping and cutting tools for grain and seed laboratories.

**Result of this step:** Using "perforated template + manual cutting main body" as the identification combination, search for professional apparatus catalogs containing actual product photos.

## Step 02 · Verify against supplier original images and the Pohl name

**Action:** Check the Kastenmüller product page and page 36 of its laboratory apparatus catalog to bind the name to the actual image.

https://kastenmueller-shop.com/769/kornschneider-nach-pohl

https://kastenmueller.com/images/004_loesungen/045_labortechnik/KASTENMUELLER_Katalog_Labortechnik.pdf

**Evidence Observation:** The product page is titled `KORNSCHNEIDER nach Pohl`, and the original product photo saved on the page corresponds to the same set of apparatus as the title image: the positions of the long handles, the flip-up cover plate, the rectangular working area, and the arrangement of the three templates on the left, right, and front are identical. Another perspective on page 36 of the catalog still shows the same main body and three templates, with text descriptions mentioning three cross-section comparison plates. Changes in angle in the catalog do not affect the structural correspondence; the webpage and this catalog both belong to supplier materials and cannot be called certifications from two independent manufacturers.

**Result of this step:** Obtained the specific type name Pohl and linked it to the apparatus in the title image via the original photo, rather than guessing a generic term for a cutter based solely on usage.

## Step 03 · Use real neighbors to check the discriminative power of the rectangular scissor-style structure

**Action:** Read the preview of printed pages 21–22 of the Pawlowski–Doemens technical book to compare the side-by-side figures of Pohl and Grobecker; then use saved university seed counting board and manufacturer microplate data to check for the most likely misidentification involving hole plates.

https://api.pageplace.de/preview/DT0400.9783486769647_A42395963/preview-9783486769647_A42395963.pdf

https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/seed_certification/seed%20tech%20agri%20index/Seed_seedtesting.html

https://www.thermofisher.com/order/catalog/product/269787

**Evidence Observation:** Figure 12 in the technical book shows the Pohl type adopting a rectangular working area and opening/closing long handles, while Figure 13 shows the Grobecker type with a circular working area and radial handles; both belong to grain cross-cutting tools, distinguished by structure rather than usage. The seed counting board shown in the university materials is a single flat plate with a lifting ring, illustrating seed dropping via sliding of plate layers and hole alignment, and lacks the cutting main body shown in the title image. The specifications and diagrams of the manufacturer's microplates are an 8×12 liquid hole array, which also cannot explain the metal long handles and three separate templates in the title image. The above comparisons only cover materials already read and do not claim to have excluded all special custom fixtures.

**Result of this step:** The Pohl naming is consistent with the visible structure, and several actual neighbors do not provide a better explanation; names of other cross-cutters without reliable images do not require forcing structural differences to be filled in.

## Step 04 · Verify translation and usage with professional catalogs before answering

**Action:** Read page 26 of the VLB LaboTech 2013 catalog and refer to the method description on page 11 of the FranceAgriMer/ARVALIS 2014 durum wheat quality report to verify the scope referred to by the Chinese apparatus name.

https://www.vlb-berlin.org/sites/default/files/2018-07/VLB-Labotech_DeliveryProgramme_2013.pdf

https://www.arvalis.fr/sites/default/files/imported_files/bat_blesdurs_fr_01_2121068826868791721.pdf

**Evidence Observation:** VLB lists this apparatus as `Barley cutter according to Pohl` and lists the cover plate and three cross-section reference plates; the agronomy report uses `farinotome de Pohl` to describe the grain cross-section inspection method. Thus, the apparatus in the figure, which clamps and cuts grains to inspect the endosperm state, can be called a Pohl-type grain cutter. Usage text helps explain the structure, but the attribution of the target photo still relies on the product page. The question does not ask for the supplier, production year, item number, or capacity, so these extra pieces of information are not written as mandatory fields.

**Result of this step:** The name, original image, and type description corroborate one another; stop retrieval.

**Formal Answer:**

Pohl-type grain cutter
